title: Socinians: God's outward and inward help
source_text: LXXXVII. Caeterum duplici ratione Deum hominum conatibus opitulari dicunt; quarum altera externa est, & vel in minando, vel in promittendo consistit: quanquam in promissis major vis sit homines Dei studio inflammandi: altera vero internum auxilium est quod tunc nobis Deus affert, quum vel promissa nobis facta, ac externis documentis confirmata animis nostris divina virtute penitius insculpit, vel pleniori voluntatis suae notitia nos instruit.
pass_a_gloss: LXXXVII. Moreover they say that God aids the endeavours of men in a twofold way; of which the one is external, & consists either in threatening, or in promising: although in the promises there is greater force for inflaming men with zeal for God: but the other is an internal help which God then brings us, when he either engraves more deeply on our minds by divine power the promises made to us, and confirmed by external proofs, or instructs us with a fuller knowledge of his will.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXXVII. They say, further, that God aids human efforts in two ways. One is outward and lies in threats or in promises, though promises have more power to fire people with devotion to God.
The other is an inward help that God gives us when, by divine power, he engraves more deeply on our minds the promises made to us and confirmed by outward proofs, or teaches us his will more fully.
